transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2025-06-25
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Verdant - CISO), Tom Wallace (Verdant - Head of Infra), Aisha Khan (Verdant - Legal), Samir Patel (Verdant - DevOps), Ellie Chen (Verdant - PM)
Links Shared: Redwood Trust Center link (provisioned during call), SOC2 PDF (to be sent), ISO 27001 cert (to be sent), Controls mapping template (CSV)

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Today we wanted to run through our SOC 2 and ISO posture, show how the Trust Center works and understand Verdant's mapping needs. Priya will cover the technical bits, I'll run through the compliance artifacts and next steps.

[00:22] Marta (Verdant): Thanks Jordan. High level - we're evaluating whether Redwood can host inference for some ePHI-adjacent flows. Key gating factors are SOC 2 scope, ISO cert, KMS options, and audit logs / retention; legal will need contractual language for data residency.

[00:40] Priya (Redwood): Great; quick agenda: SOC2 evidence and scope, Trust Center demo, controls mapping process, encryption and KMS modes (hosted vs private), SSO/RBAC pattern, audit logs and retention. We'll leave time for Q/A.

[01:05] Tom (Verdant): Quick clarifier - when you say SOC2 Type II, is that Redwood's entire platform or just hosted API? We need to know if dedicated or private deployments are covered.

[01:20] Jordan: Good question. Our SOC2 Type II covers our hosted Redwood API and the core control plane. For Dedicated we provide a controls extension and for Private (VPC/on-prem) we offer an evidence package plus self-hosted controls guidance. We'll send the exact scope doc; in short hosted = in scope, dedicated = contractually extended, private = customer-managed but we provide mapping and docs.

[01:55] Marta: Okay, helpful. Is the SOC2 report redacted? Will we get a full report or is it a redacted version?

[02:10] Jordan: We typically provide a redacted SOC2 Type II report to prospects and grant read-only Trust Center access for validated customers; the Trust Center contains the control testing details, policy docs, and artifact index. For a contract, we can arrange a more in-depth SSAE SOC listing. We'll attach the redacted PDF after the call.

[02:40] Priya: I'll jump into Trust Center - (slight cough) excuse me - I'm sharing my screen. The Trust Center gives a controls matrix, mapping to SOC2 and ISO 27001, and you can export artifacts. Note some artifact names in the UI are auto-generated and may show slight typos, we fix as we go but this is normal.

[03:10] [Screen share walkthrough w/ short pauses - transcript sometimes misreads "trust center" as "trust censer"]

[04:00] Priya: Here's the controls export. It maps our control IDs to SOC2 criteria and ISO clauses. We also include implementation notes - e.g., for encryption at rest we point to our KMS integration doc. The export is a CSV you can download and ingest into your GRC.

[04:30] Samir (Verdant): Do you provide a control mapping we can ingest directly into our Archer/GRC? CSV is fine but can we get field names?

[04:45] Priya: Yes we'll provide a CSV with consistent column names; we'll also attach a sample mapping to Verdant's control names if you share a few sample controls.

[05:10] Ellie (Verdant): On data residency - are there region locks for hosted? Our data needs to stay in US regions for now.

[05:25] Jordan: Hosted API supports regional routing and we can pin to US regions. If you need strict contractual residency we recommend Dedicated or Private. We'll include region SLA language in the follow up.

[05:50] Marta: Encryption - specifically keys. Do you offer customer-managed keys (BYOK)? HSM?

[06:05] Priya: In hosted mode we use cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) and provide customer-managed key options for Dedicated and Private. For Private deployments you can integrate your HSM or KMS via our KMS connector. Currently we support BYOK via Cloud KMS and can discuss HSM proxies for on-prem HSMs. We'll need to scope exact connector work during the follow-up.

[06:40] Tom: How are encryption keys rotated and who has access? We have strict separation of duties.

[06:55] Priya: Key rotation policies are documented; for customer-managed keys you control rotation. For Redwood-managed keys we enforce role-based access and AWS KMS policies, with audit logs sent to our CMK audit stream. We'll provide the KMS controls doc.

[07:30] Aisha (Verdant): From a legal perspective - where are audit logs stored and how long do you retain them? We might need 7 years for some regs.

[07:45] Jordan: Default audit log retention in hosted is 90 days for high-fidelity logs, with aggregated metrics longer depending on plan. For Dedicated and Private you have options to export and retain logs in your SIEM indefinitely. We often provide a log forwarding integration to Splunk/ELK/Datadog. We'll include sample log schemas and retention options.

[08:20] Samir: What's the log format? JSON lines? Any Kafka streams or syslog?

[08:35] Priya: We emit structured JSON events and support HTTPS push, Kafka, and syslog collectors depending on deployment. We'll share schema examples.

[09:00] Marta: Controls mapping - can Redwood map which evidence artifacts satisfy which Verdant control IDs?

[09:15] Priya: Yes; our Trust Center export supports mapping to your control IDs. We can do an initial mapping in the pilot phase and hand off a completed CSV for your GRC team.

[09:40] Ellie: About PHI - is Redwood willing to sign BAA?

[09:55] Jordan: We have customers that process PHI under BAAs in Dedicated and Private modes. For hosted we evaluate on a case-by-case basis and typically recommend Dedicated/Private for PHI. Legal will share standard BAA language; we'll respond with redlined terms if needed.

[10:15] Aisha: We'll need to see where the log files and telemetry live too - sometimes telemetry includes metadata we need to treat as PHI.

[10:30] Priya: Good point - our docs call out what's considered telemetry vs content. For content that includes PHI we recommend Private or strict contract terms with hosted and explicit data handling clauses.

[11:00] [Brief cross talk - audio glitch / transcription reads "K V cache" as "K V catche"]

[11:25] Tom: On the technical deep dive - what does an integration look like if we keep inference on your dedicated pool but keys in our KMS?

[11:40] Priya: Typical pattern: requests route to Dedicated inference nodes; payloads are encrypted at rest; decryption keys are referenced via KMS APIs with short-lived data keys. We support envelope encryption so sensitive payloads never persist in plaintext. For extra assurance we can add a KMS proxy in your VPC.

[12:10] Samir: Any changes needed on our side for tokenization or prefix caching? We run a lot of prompt templates and want deterministic behavior for auditing.

[12:25] Priya: No changes required for prompt behavior; we log request metadata (request id, model, route, time) and you can choose to log full request bodies if allowed. For privacy we recommend a redaction pipeline - we can show an architecture for that.

[12:55] Marta: Can we get an export of the controls that map to ISO 27001 clauses? Our internal ISO lead wants to see the exact clause mapping.

[13:10] Jordan: We'll attach an ISO mapping CSV and the ISO 27001 cert. Also we can provide the scope doc that lists which services are covered.

[13:35] Aisha: About evidence - how do we get the raw artifacts? For example pen test reports, config snapshots, and access logs.

[13:50] Jordan: Pen test reports are redacted; config snapshots and access logs are available via the Trust Center or via S3 export for Dedicated/Private. For redacted pen test we provide executive summary; full reports can be shown in a controlled review if needed.

[14:15] Priya: I'll note that some artifact filenames in our older exports have minor typos - "confg" instead of "config" occasionally - it's on our backlog to normalize but I want to be transparent about what you might see.

[14:40] Tom: Sounds good. For the pilot, we'd want a checklist: artifact access, controls mapping, KMS integration test, and a small benchmark to validate latency.

[14:55] Jordan: That's reasonable. Proposed pilot plan: 1) Provide Trust Center access + SOC2/ISO docs, 2) do a controls mapping workshop, 3) KMS test with sample keys, 4) run a small POC with a 2-week sample to validate logs/latency. We'll put this in the follow up email.

[15:25] Marta: If we decide on Dedicated, are there SLA commitments for key rotation and retention?

[15:40] Jordan: Yes Dedicated contracts include configurable SLAs for uptime and retention, and we include controls language for key rotation windows. We'll surface sample SLA clauses.

[16:00] Aisha: Any show-stoppers you can think of for PHI?

[16:15] Priya: Main considerations: where content is stored, who can access keys, and legal controls. With Dedicated/Private + BYOK + BAA those are addressable. Hosted is more constrained but sometimes still possible with contractual protections.

[16:40] [Silence; background noise; brief microphone adjustment - transcript shows "um" and filler]

[17:05] Jordan: Okay quick recap - we'll send SOC2 PDF and ISO cert, Priya will provision Trust Center access and export a controls CSV, Samir to send log retention/forwarding details, Aisha will share legal constraints. We'll schedule the KMS deep-dive next week.

[17:35] Tom: One last technical Q - Do you have an audit trail for admin actions in the control plane? We need to prove separation of duties.

[17:50] Priya: Yes, all control plane admin actions are logged: who, what, when, and we persist change diffs for configuration. We can export admin audit logs to your SIEM.

[18:10] Marta: Perfect. Anything else?

[18:20] Ellie: No, thanks. We'll review the artifacts once you send them.

[18:30] Jordan: Thanks all, we'll follow up with links and the pilot plan.

[18:40] [Call ends - small wrap-up chatter, some crosstalk]

Notes on transcript quality: Automated transcript has a few mis-transcriptions (e.g., "trust censer", "K V cache"), occasional missing punctuation and filler words. Some proper nouns may be slightly off.

Artifacts to send (post-call): SOC2 Type II redacted PDF, ISO 27001 cert, Trust Center read-only invite link, controls mapping CSV template, KMS integration doc, sample audit log schema.
